# Book I, Proposition 13

*Angles on a straight line equal two right angles*

> If a straight line set up on a straight line make angles, it will make either two right angles or angles equal to two right angles.

<p align="center"><img src="../../figures/I/13-idea.svg" alt="However one straight line stands on another, the two angles it makes (red and blue) together equal two right angles (yellow)." width="420"></p>

<p align="center"><em>However one straight line stands on another, the two angles it makes (red and blue) together equal two right angles (yellow).</em></p>

## Euclid's proof

<p align="center"><img src="../../figures/I/13.svg" alt="Euclid's figure for Proposition I.13, with Heath's letters" width="360"></p>

For let any straight line AB set up on the straight line CD make the angles CBA, ABD;

I say that the angles CBA, ABD are either two right angles or equal to two right angles.

Now, if the angle CBA is equal to the angle ABD,

they are two right angles. [Def. 10]

But, if not, let BE be drawn from the point B at right angles to CD; [I. 11]

therefore the angles CBE, EBD are two right angles.

Then, since the angle CBE is equal to the two angles CBA, ABE,

let the angle EBD be added to each;

therefore the angles CBE, EBD are equal to the three angles CBA, ABE, EBD. [C.N. 2]

Again, since the angle DBA is equal to the two angles DBE, EBA,

let the angle ABC be added to each;

therefore the angles DBA, ABC are equal to the three angles DBE, EBA, ABC. [C.N. 2]

But the angles CBE, EBD were also proved equal to the same three angles;

and things which are equal to the same thing are also equal to one another; [C.N. 1]

therefore the angles CBE, EBD are also equal to the angles DBA, ABC.

But the angles CBE, EBD are two right angles;

therefore the angles DBA, ABC are also equal to two right angles.

Therefore etc.

Q. E. D.

```lean
/-! ## What Euclid reads off the figure -/

/-- Euclid's figure, seen from the other end of `CD`. If `BA` falls within the angle
`CBE` (`A` on `E`'s side of `BC`, and on `C`'s side of `BE`), and `CB` is produced to
`D`, then `BE` falls within the angle `DBA`: `E` is on `A`'s side of `BD`, and on
`D`'s side of `BA`.

The first is the same side of the same straight line. For the second, the three
straight lines `BC`, `BA`, `BE` through `B` divide the plane into six regions, and
since `A` lies between `C` and `E` as seen from `B`, the straight line `BA` separates
`C` from `E` (System E, Triple incidence 1); it also separates `C` from `D` (Pasch 3),
and a straight line has only two sides (Same side 5). -/
theorem Prop13.within {A B C D E : Point} (hCBD : Between C B D) (hAE : SameSideOf A E B C)
    (hAC : SameSideOf A C B E) : SameSideOf E A B D ∧ SameSideOf E D B A := by
  have hBC : B ≠ C := hAE.1
  have hBD : B ≠ D := (ne_of_between (between_symm hCBD)).symm
  have hBE : B ≠ E := hAC.1
  have hBA : B ≠ A := hAC.triangle.ne₁₃
  obtain ⟨L, hB_L, hC_L⟩ := Postulate1 B C hBC
  have hD_L : OnLine D L := on_line_of_between hCBD hC_L hB_L
  obtain ⟨M, hB_M, hE_M⟩ := Postulate1 B E hBE
  obtain ⟨N, hB_N, hA_N⟩ := Postulate1 B A hBA
  have hAE_L : SameSide A E L := hAE.sameSide hB_L hC_L
  have hAC_M : SameSide A C M := hAC.sameSide hB_M hE_M
  have hA_L : ¬ OnLine A L := not_on_line_of_same_side hAE_L
  have hA_M : ¬ OnLine A M := not_on_line_of_same_side hAC_M
  refine ⟨SameSideOf.of_line hBD hB_L hD_L (same_side_symm hAE_L), ?_⟩
  /- BA separates C from E (Triple incidence 1) ... -/
  have hCE_N : ¬ SameSide C E N :=
    triple_incidence1 hB_L hB_N hB_M hC_L hA_N hE_M hAE_L (same_side_symm hAC_M)
  /- ... and C from D (Pasch 3). -/
  have hCD_N : ¬ SameSide C D N := pasch3 hCBD hB_N
  /- None of C, D, E is on BA: else BA would be BC, or BE, and A would be on it. -/
  have hC_N : ¬ OnLine C N := fun hC => hA_L (line_unique hBC hB_N hC hB_L hC_L ▸ hA_N)
  have hD_N : ¬ OnLine D N := fun hD => hA_L (line_unique hBD hB_N hD hB_L hD_L ▸ hA_N)
  have hE_N : ¬ OnLine E N := fun hE => hA_M (line_unique hBE hB_N hE hB_M hE_M ▸ hA_N)
  /- So E, not on C's side of BA, is on D's (Same side 5). -/
  have hDE_N : SameSide D E N :=
    same_side_of_opposite_sides ⟨hC_N, hD_N, hCD_N⟩ ⟨hC_N, hE_N, hCE_N⟩
  exact SameSideOf.of_line hBA hB_N hA_N (same_side_symm hDE_N)

/-- Which way `AB` leans. With `BE` at right angles to `CD`, on `A`'s side of it, and
the angles `CBA`, `ABD` unequal, `A` lies on `C`'s side of `BE` or on `D`'s.

It is not on `BE` itself: being on `E`'s side of `CD`, it would lie on the ray from
`B` through `E`, and then the angles `CBA`, `ABD` would be the right angles `CBE`,
`EBD` themselves, and equal (Diagram-angle 4). `C` and `D` are on opposite sides of
`BE` (Pasch 3), and a straight line has only two sides (Same side 5). -/
theorem Prop13.cases {A B C D E : Point} (hCBD : Between C B D) (hEA : SameSideOf E A C D)
    (hCBE : ∠ C B E = ∟) (hEBD : ∠ E B D = ∟) (hne : ∠ C B A ≠ ∠ A B D) :
    SameSideOf A C B E ∨ SameSideOf A D B E := by
  have hCB : C ≠ B := ne_of_between hCBD
  have hDB : D ≠ B := ne_of_between (between_symm hCBD)
  obtain ⟨L, hC_L, hD_L⟩ := Postulate1 C D hEA.1
  have hB_L : OnLine B L := on_line_of_between_ends hCBD hC_L hD_L
  have hEA_L : SameSide E A L := hEA.sameSide hC_L hD_L
  have hE_L : ¬ OnLine E L := not_on_line_of_same_side hEA_L
  have hBE : B ≠ E := fun e => hE_L (e ▸ hB_L)
  obtain ⟨M, hB_M, hE_M⟩ := Postulate1 B E hBE
  have hC_M : ¬ OnLine C M := fun hC => hE_L (line_unique hCB hC hB_M hC_L hB_L ▸ hE_M)
  have hD_M : ¬ OnLine D M := fun hD => hE_L (line_unique hDB hD hB_M hD_L hB_L ▸ hE_M)
  have hA_M : ¬ OnLine A M := by
    intro hA
    have hAB : A ≠ B := fun e => not_on_line_of_same_side (same_side_symm hEA_L) (e ▸ hB_L)
    /- A would be on the ray from B through E, not behind B (Pasch 3,
       `OnRay.of_sameSideOf`). -/
    have hA_ray : OnRay A B E :=
      OnRay.of_sameSideOf (SameSideOf.of_line hCB.symm hB_L hC_L (same_side_symm hEA_L))
        ⟨M, hB_M, hE_M, hA⟩ hAB
    apply hne
    rw [angle_onRay_right hA_ray hCB, angle_onRay_left hA_ray hDB, hCBE, hEBD]
  rcases same_side_or hC_M hD_M hA_M (pasch3 hCBD hB_M) with h | h
  · exact Or.inl (SameSideOf.of_line hBE hB_M hE_M (same_side_symm h))
  · exact Or.inr (SameSideOf.of_line hBE hB_M hE_M (same_side_symm h))

/-- If a straight line set up on a straight line make angles, it will make either two right angles
or angles equal to two right angles. -/
theorem Prop13 {A B C D : Point} (hCBD : Between C B D) (hA : ¬ Collinear C D A) :
    ∠ C B A + ∠ A B D = ∟ + ∟ := by
  -- For let any straight line AB set up on the straight line CD make the angles CBA, ABD;
  /- The straight line CD, with B on it between C and D, and A off it. -/
  have hCB : C ≠ B := ne_of_between hCBD
  have hDB : D ≠ B := ne_of_between (between_symm hCBD)
  have hCD : C ≠ D := ne_of_between_ends hCBD
  obtain ⟨CD, hC_CD, hD_CD⟩ := Postulate1 C D hCD
  have hB_CD : OnLine B CD := on_line_of_between_ends hCBD hC_CD hD_CD
  have hA_CD : ¬ OnLine A CD := fun h => hA ⟨CD, hC_CD, hD_CD, h⟩
  have hAB : A ≠ B := fun e => hA_CD (e ▸ hB_CD)
  -- I say that the angles CBA, ABD are either two right angles or equal to two right angles.
  /- "Two right angles": each of them is right. "Equal to two right angles": together
     they make two. In Lean a right angle has one size, `∟`, by Postulate 4, so the
     first is a case of the second, and the statement asks only for the second. -/
  -- Now, if the angle CBA is equal to the angle ABD,
  by_cases heq : ∠ C B A = ∠ A B D
  -- they are two right angles. [Def. 10]
  /- Definition 10 says each is right, for they are adjacent angles (A is off the
     straight line CD); Postulate 4 says each is then equal to `∟`. -/
  · have hCBA : ∠ C B A = ∟ :=
      Postulate4 ⟨D, hCBD, Triangle.of_line hC_CD hB_CD hCB hA_CD, heq⟩
    have hABD : ∠ A B D = ∟ := heq.symm.trans hCBA
    rw [hCBA, hABD]
  -- But, if not, let BE be drawn from the point B at right angles to CD; [I. 11]
  /- I.11 draws BE on whichever side of CD we ask; we ask for A's side. -/
  obtain ⟨E, hEA, hperp⟩ := Prop11 (A := C) (B := D) (C := B) (Q := A) hCD
    ⟨CD, hC_CD, hD_CD, hB_CD⟩ hA
  have hEB : E ≠ B := fun e => hEA.triangle.off_line hC_CD hD_CD (e ▸ hB_CD)
  -- therefore the angles CBE, EBD are two right angles.
  have hCBE : ∠ C B E = ∟ := hperp C ⟨CD, hC_CD, hD_CD, hC_CD⟩ hCB
  have hDBE : ∠ D B E = ∟ := hperp D ⟨CD, hC_CD, hD_CD, hD_CD⟩ hDB
  have hEBD : ∠ E B D = ∟ := by rw [angle_symm hEB hDB]; exact hDBE
  have hEBC : ∠ E B C = ∟ := by rw [angle_symm hEB hCB]; exact hCBE
  /- In Euclid's figure BA falls within the angle CBE: A is on E's side of BC, and on
     C's side of BE. If A is on D's side of BE instead, the figure is Euclid's with C
     and D exchanged (`Prop13.cases`), so we give his argument for either naming of
     the ends of CD, and use it below. A is on E's side of CD, as I.11 put it, and so
     of BC and of BD, which are the same straight line. -/
  have hAE_BC : SameSideOf A E B C :=
    SameSideOf.of_line hCB.symm hB_CD hC_CD (same_side_symm (hEA.sameSide hC_CD hD_CD))
  have hAE_BD : SameSideOf A E B D :=
    SameSideOf.of_line hDB.symm hB_CD hD_CD (same_side_symm (hEA.sameSide hC_CD hD_CD))
  have two_right : ∀ {C D : Point}, Between C B D → ∠ C B E = ∟ → ∠ E B D = ∟ →
      SameSideOf A E B C → SameSideOf A C B E → ∠ D B A + ∠ A B C = ∟ + ∟ := by
    intro C D hCBD hCBE hEBD hAE hAC
    have hCB : C ≠ B := ne_of_between hCBD
    have hDB : D ≠ B := ne_of_between (between_symm hCBD)
    -- Then, since the angle CBE is equal to the two angles CBA, ABE,
    /- BA falls within the angle CBE. -/
    have hCBE_sum : ∠ C B E = ∠ C B A + ∠ A B E := angle_add_of_within hAE hAC
    -- let the angle EBD be added to each;
    -- therefore the angles CBE, EBD are equal to the three angles CBA, ABE, EBD. [C.N. 2]
    have hthree : ∠ C B E + ∠ E B D = ∠ C B A + ∠ A B E + ∠ E B D :=
      CommonNotion2 hCBE_sum rfl
    -- Again, since the angle DBA is equal to the two angles DBE, EBA,
    /- And so BE falls within the angle DBA (`Prop13.within`). -/
    obtain ⟨hEA', hED⟩ := Prop13.within hCBD hAE hAC
    have hDBA_sum : ∠ D B A = ∠ D B E + ∠ E B A := angle_add_of_within hEA' hED
    -- let the angle ABC be added to each;
    -- therefore the angles DBA, ABC are equal to the three angles DBE, EBA, ABC. [C.N. 2]
    have hthree' : ∠ D B A + ∠ A B C = ∠ D B E + ∠ E B A + ∠ A B C :=
      CommonNotion2 hDBA_sum rfl
    -- But the angles CBE, EBD were also proved equal to the same three angles;
    /- The same three, named from the other end and added in the other order: the
       angle CBA is the angle ABC (System E, Metric 4), and the order of adding does
       not matter (a tacit law of magnitudes). -/
    have hsame : ∠ C B E + ∠ E B D = ∠ D B E + ∠ E B A + ∠ A B C := by
      rw [hthree, angle_symm hCB hAB, angle_symm hAB hEB, angle_symm hEB hDB,
        add_comm (∠ A B C + ∠ E B A), add_comm (∠ A B C), ← add_assoc]
    -- and things which are equal to the same thing are also equal to one another; [C.N. 1]
    -- therefore the angles CBE, EBD are also equal to the angles DBA, ABC.
    have hequal : ∠ C B E + ∠ E B D = ∠ D B A + ∠ A B C := CommonNotion1 hsame hthree'
    -- But the angles CBE, EBD are two right angles;
    have hright : ∠ C B E + ∠ E B D = ∟ + ∟ := by rw [hCBE, hEBD]
    -- therefore the angles DBA, ABC are also equal to two right angles.
    exact hequal.symm.trans hright
  -- Therefore etc.
  rcases Prop13.cases hCBD hEA hCBE hEBD heq with hAC | hAD
  · /- Euclid's figure. -/
    rw [angle_symm hCB hAB, angle_symm hAB hDB, add_comm (∠ A B C)]
    exact two_right hCBD hCBE hEBD hAE_BC hAC
  · /- Euclid's figure, with C and D exchanged. -/
    exact two_right (between_symm hCBD) hDBE hEBC hAE_BD hAD
  -- Q. E. D.
```

**Reading the figure**

- [`between_cases`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L74): Of three different points on a straight line, one is between the other two. (Between 6)
- [`between_of_between_left`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L66): If `B` is between `A` and `C`, and `D` is between `A` and `B`, then `D` is between `A` and `C`. (Between 4)
- [`between_of_between_right`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L70): If `B` is between `A` and `C`, and `C` is between `B` and `D`, then `B` is between `A` and `D`. (Between 5)
- [`between_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L43): If `B` is between `A` and `C`, it is between `C` and `A`. (Between 1)
- [`centre_inside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L35): The centre of a circle is inside it. (Generalities 3)
- [`circles_meet`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L201): If each circle passes through a point inside the other, the circles cut one another. This is the step Euclid takes for granted in I.1. (Intersection 5)
- [`circles_meet_same_side`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L81): Two circles that cut one another do so on each side of the straight line through their centres. (Intersections 8)
- [`exists_point`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L26): Let a point be taken. (Points 1)
- [`exists_point_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L38): Let a point be taken between `B` and `C`. (Points 3)
- [`inside_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L161): A circle is "convex": between two points on or inside it, every point is inside. (Circle 2)
- [`line_circle_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L69): A straight line through a point `B` inside a circle, heading out to a point `C` outside it, cuts the circle between `B` and `C`. (Intersections 4)
- [`line_circle_beyond`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Constructions.lean#L75): A straight line through a point `B` inside a circle, produced beyond `B` away from `C`, cuts the circle there. (Intersections 5)
- [`line_unique`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L28): Two points determine a straight line. (Generalities 1)
- [`lines_meet_of_opposite_sides`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L179): A straight line joining points on opposite sides of `L` crosses `L`. (Intersection 1)
- [`ne_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L46): A point between two others differs from the first. (Between 1)
- [`ne_of_between_ends`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L49): The ends of a finite straight line differ. (Between 1)
- [`not_between_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L52): If `B` is between `A` and `C`, then `A` is not between `B` and `C`. (Between 1)
- [`not_between_of_between_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L79): If `B` is between `A` and `C`, and also between `A` and `D`, then `B` is not between `C` and `D`: `C` and `D` lie on the same side of `B`. (Between 7)
- [`not_on_line_of_same_side`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L92): Points on one side of a line are not on it. (Same side 3)
- [`on_line_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L56): A straight line through `A` and `B`, with `B` between `A` and `C`, passes through `C`. (Between 2)
- [`on_line_of_between_ends`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L61): A straight line through `A` and `C` passes through every point between them. (Between 3)
- [`pasch2`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L111): If `B` is between `A` and `C`, `A` is on `L` and `B` is off it, then `B` and `C` are on the same side of `L`: a straight line that leaves `L` at `A` does not cross it again. (Pasch 2)
- [`pasch3`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L114): A line through a point between `A` and `C` separates them. (Pasch 3)
- [`pasch4`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L119): If two different straight lines `L` and `M` meet at `B`, and `A` and `C` are points of `M`, different from each other and from `B`, that are not on the same side of `L`, then `B` is between `A` and `C`. (Pasch 4)
- [`same_side_or`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L99): A straight line has only two sides. (Same side 5)
- [`same_side_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L89): If `A` is on the same side of a straight line as `B`, then `B` is on the same side as `A`. (Same side 2)
- [`same_side_trans`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L96): Two points on the same side of a straight line as a third point are on the same side as each other. (Same side 4)
- [`triple_incidence1`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L131): Take `B` on `L`, `C` on `M` and `D` on `N`, three straight lines through `A`. If `C` lies within the angle `BAD` (on `D`'s side of `L` and on `B`'s side of `N`), then `B` and `D` are not on the same side of `M`: the straight line `AC` separates them. (Triple incidence 1)
- [`triple_incidence2`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Diagram.lean#L139): Take `B` on `L`, `C` on `M` and `D` on `N`, three straight lines through `A`, with `B` other than `A` and `D` off `M`. If `C` and `D` are on the same side of `L`, and `B` and `D` are not on the same side of `M`, then `B` and `C` are on the same side of `N`: `C` lies within the angle `BAD`. (Triple incidence 2)

**Lengths, angles and areas**

- [`angle_add_of_inside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L54): If `D` lies within the angle `BAC`, then `BAC` is made up of `BAD` and `DAC`. (Diagram-angle 2)
- [`angle_eq_of_same_rays`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L72): The angle doesn't change if its arms are traced through other points on the same rays. (Diagram-angle 4)
- [`angle_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L26): The angle `ABC` is the angle `CBA`. (Metric 4)

- [`area_rotate`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L35): The triangle `ABC` is the triangle `CAB`. (Metric 8)
- [`area_swap`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L38): The triangle `ABC` is the triangle `ACB`. (Metric 8)
- [`eq_of_len_eq_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L17): A finite straight line with distinct ends has length. (Metric 1)
- [`inside_of_len_lt`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L33): A point nearer the centre than the circumference is inside. (Diagram-segment 4)
- [`len_add_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L21): If `B` is between `A` and `C`, then `AB` and `BC` together make up `AC`. (Diagram-segment 1)
- [`len_lt_of_inside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L37): A point inside is nearer the centre than the circumference. (Diagram-segment 4)

**Superposition**

- [`superposition`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Superposition.lean#L30): **Superposition.** The triangle `ABC` can be applied to the straight line `L` with `A` on `D`, `B` on the ray from `D` through `G`, and `C` on the side of `L` where `H` is, without changing any side or angle.

**Laws of magnitude**

- [`add_assoc`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L22): Adding is associative. (System E §3.5)
- [`add_comm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L25): Adding is commutative. (System E §3.5)
- [`add_lt_add_right`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L44): Adding the same thing to both sides keeps "less than". (System E §3.5)
- [`add_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L28): Adding nothing changes nothing. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_irrefl`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L31): No magnitude is less than itself. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_trans`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L34): "Less than" is transitive. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_trichotomy`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L38): Of two magnitudes, one is less, or they are equal, or the other is less. (System E §3.5)
- [`not_lt_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L41): Nothing is less than zero. (System E §3.5)

</details>

## Mishnah

**Two right angles, or equal to two.** Euclid's enunciation offers a choice: "either two right angles or angles equal to two right angles". The first is the case of Definition 10, where the two angles are equal and so each is right. In Lean a right angle has one size, `∟`, because Postulate 4 says that all right angles are equal, so the statement keeps only the second form, ∠ CBA + ∠ ABD = ∟ + ∟. The first case then needs one citation more than Euclid gives: Definition 10, which he cites, makes each angle right, and Postulate 4, which he doesn't, makes each `∟` (I.11 brings it in as well); Isaac Todhunter points out its quiet work under I.14.

**Which way AB leans.** Euclid draws AB leaning towards C, so that BA falls within the right angle CBE and BE within the angle DBA, and both of his "since the angle … is equal to the two angles" read this off the figure. Lean wants each said: `angle_add_of_within` (System E, Diagram-angle 2) makes an angle the sum of two when a straight line falls within it, and `Prop13.within` shows that BE falls within DBA. If AB leans towards D, the figure is Euclid's with C and D exchanged, so the Lean gives his argument once and uses it either way (`Prop13.cases`). A cannot lie on BE itself, for then the angles CBA, ABD would be the right angles CBE, EBD over again, and equal. And BE must be drawn on A's side of CD, which the statement of I.11 lets us choose.

**"Added to each."** Heath's one note on I.13 is about a phrase. "Let the angle EBD be added to each" is "literally 'let the angle EBD be added (so as to be) common,' κοινὴ προσκείσθω ἡ ὑπὸ ΕΒΔ", and "'Let the common angle EBD be added' is clearly an inaccurate translation, for the angle is not common before it is added, i.e. the κοινή is proleptic" (Heath, vol. 1, p. 276). The Lean says it the Greek way: `CommonNotion2 hCBE_sum rfl` adds the angle EBD to both sides, and the `rfl` is there because it is one and the same angle, common to both.

**The modern way.** Put B at 0 in the complex plane, D at 1, C at −1 and A at e^{iθ} with 0 < θ < π. The angle ABD is arg e^{iθ} = θ, the angle CBA is arg(−e^{−iθ}) = π − θ, and together they make π: two right angles.
